Synopsis:
    Treasury Secretary Bessent publicly endorsed leveraging the U.S. balance sheet as a foreign policy instrument, citing Argentina as a test case where financial support was deployed to stabilize currency and back the Milei government ahead of midterms. He also disclosed U.S. involvement in a joint yen-buying intervention with Japan on July 31, claiming direct insight into Bank of Japan policy intentions. The article frames these as part of a broader Trump administration doctrine using financial resources, tariffs, and military action to project U.S. influence — particularly across the Western hemisphere.
